issues.legal_issue: Related proceedings concerning the same land and seeking identical relief should be heard and disposed of together when they are pending at the same time and can be joined.
material_facts: Two proceedings between the same parties concerned different portions of the same land and sought identical relief under the same statute.
Both proceedings were pending simultaneously, but they were tried separately and resulted in conflicting decisions.
issues.conclusion: The proceedings should have been clubbed for disposal on the merits; the court could have done so on its own motion under Order II Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Order II Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits joinder of causes of action. Where related proceedings satisfy its attributes, the court may club them to avoid conflicting decisions and prejudice to the parties.

rule.if: parallel_related_proceedings and same_parties_and_land and identical_relief_sought and proceedings_pending_simultaneously

predicates.parallel_related_proceedings: More than one proceeding concerning related claims is pending before a court.
predicates.same_parties_and_land: The proceedings involve the same parties and the same land, or portions of it.
predicates.identical_relief_sought: The claimants seek the same kind of relief in each proceeding.
predicates.proceedings_pending_simultaneously: The proceedings are pending at the same time.

issues.definition: When related proceedings involving the same parties and land seek identical relief and are pending together, they should be disposed of jointly.

issues.legal_issue: State authorities involved in one of two related proceedings should also be joined in the other when their participation is material to the dispute.
material_facts: The District Collector and the land-ceiling authority were parties to the first proceeding but were omitted from the second proceeding concerning another portion of the same land.
The Collector had disputed the claimants’ title and referred to government records in the first proceeding.
The omission meant that no response from the Collector was filed in the second proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The District Collector and the land-ceiling authority should be added as parties to the second proceeding and given an opportunity to file counter-affidavits.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that joining the state authorities in both related proceedings was necessary for their proper disposal and to maintain parity between them.

predicates.related_land_proceedings: Two proceedings concern related claims to portions of the same land.
predicates.state_authorities_participated_in_one_pr: State authorities were made parties to one of the related proceedings.
predicates.state_authorities_omitted_from_another: Those authorities were not made parties to another related proceeding.

issues.definition: When state authorities participate in one of two related land proceedings but are omitted from the other, they should be joined in the latter proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: Maintainability and limitation objections to applications under the land-grabbing law must be decided along with the other issues.
material_facts: The claimants filed two applications under the land-grabbing law.
The respondent raised a limitation plea in one application.
The courts below did not decide the maintainability and limitation issues concerning the applications.
issues.conclusion: The maintainability of the applications and the issue of limitation in filing them should be decided along with the other issues.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that maintainability and limitation are issues requiring determination in proceedings under the Andhra Pradesh Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 1982, together with the other issues arising in those proceedings.

predicates.land_grabbing_application: A party has brought an application under a law addressing land grabbing.
predicates.maintainability_or_limitation_is_in_issu: A question has arisen about whether the application can be maintained or whether it was filed in time.

issues.definition: If a land-grabbing application raises a maintainability or limitation issue, that issue must be decided with the other issues.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court exercising supervisory jurisdiction cannot decide a challenge to a Special Court judgment as though it were a first appellate court by reappreciating the entire evidence.
material_facts: The High Court considered writ petitions under Article 227 challenging judgments of the Special Court.
In reversing one judgment, the High Court appreciated the entire evidence as a first appellate court.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should have decided the writ petition within the scope and limits of its jurisdiction under Article 227, rather than deciding it as an appellate court.
issues.legal_principle: Article 227 confers supervisory jurisdiction, which is not equivalent to appellate jurisdiction. The judgment refers generally to a series of Supreme Court decisions explaining that scope, but names no earlier case.

predicates.supervisory_writ_challenges_special_cour: A writ petition invoking supervisory jurisdiction challenges a judgment of a Special Court.
predicates.high_court_reappreciates_entire_evidence: The High Court reassesses the entire evidentiary record as if deciding an appeal.

issues.definition: When a supervisory writ challenges a Special Court judgment, the High Court must not reassess the entire evidence as an appellate court.

issues.legal_issue: Unsatisfactory trials that prejudice parties through separate decisions in related proceedings, material party omissions, unresolved threshold issues, or improper appellate-style supervisory review warrant setting aside the judgments and remanding the proceedings for fresh determination.
material_facts: The two related proceedings were tried separately and produced conflicting decisions.
State authorities who had disputed the claimants’ title in one proceeding were omitted from the other.
The maintainability and limitation issues were not decided.
The High Court reappreciated the evidence as though exercising appellate jurisdiction under Article 227.
The Supreme Court found that the trial was unsatisfactory and prejudicial, and chose not to decide the underlying ownership and possession disputes.
issues.conclusion: The judgments of the High Court and Special Court were set aside, and both proceedings were remanded to the Special Court for a fresh determination on the merits, with the proceedings to be clubbed and the omitted authorities added as parties. The Supreme Court made no finding on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied Order II Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure to the joinder of related causes of action, considered the requirements of the Andhra Pradesh Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 1982, and applied the limits of supervisory jurisdiction under Article 227. It held that the combined procedural deficiencies made a fresh, joint determination necessary; no particular earlier case was named in the judgment.

rule.if: land_grabbing_proceedings and related_cases_decided_separately and state_authorities_omitted_from_related_case and threshold_issues_unresolved and supervisory_review_exceeded and trial_caused_prejudice

predicates.land_grabbing_proceedings: The proceedings are applications under a law addressing land grabbing.
predicates.related_cases_decided_separately: Related proceedings that could have been heard together were decided separately.
predicates.state_authorities_omitted_from_related_c: State authorities material to one proceeding were omitted from a related proceeding.
predicates.threshold_issues_unresolved: Issues about maintainability or limitation were left undecided.
predicates.supervisory_review_exceeded: A court exercising supervisory jurisdiction decided the challenge as though it were an appeal.
predicates.trial_caused_prejudice: The way the proceedings were tried caused prejudice to a party.

issues.definition: When related land-grabbing proceedings are tried separately, material authorities are omitted, threshold issues remain unresolved, supervisory review exceeds its bounds, and the trial causes prejudice, the judgments must be set aside and the proceedings remanded for a joint fresh decision.
